questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: McGill is an old and prestigious university in North America with a great reputation. I had already been on exchange to Paris, so I wanted to go somewhere outside of Europe this time. I had visited the US approximately ten times but I had never been to Canada, so I thought it would be fun to explore. In comparison, Canada is much safer than the US, and Montreal is an old city with a fascinating colonial history. I also saw my exchange as an opportunity to be more outdoorsy (I have hiked and skied a lot this past semester) and to learn a bit of French.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. They had some webinars for new students that I watched before coming here. They also write everything on their intranet and they will send you lots and lots of emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nearly none. They offered almost no orientation as I arrived for the Winter semester (starting Jan 4th). They only invited new exchange students to one pizza night on the second day of school – which was overwhelming and unstructured – and a brunch on the Sunday of week 1. No follow ups or future events. No facebook or WhatsApp groups. So it was sort of difficult to meet new people - especially because non-exchange students were quite young and already had their established friend groups. Sadly this meant that I mostly hung out with other Danish students and with my roommate and her friends.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I ended up living with someone that I had briefly met in Copenhagen a few years prior. Remembering that she was a fulltime student at McGill, I sent her a message when I found out that I would be going here and it turned out that she had a room available. 

If you don't have an international network, I would suggest using facebook groups as that seems to be what most of my friends had done.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The standards for what is considered a decent apartment are quite low here, I think, compared to Copenhagen. The apartments that I have visited are all pre-furnished with old and broken furniture and they need some new paint. The kitchens have old appliances and, in my kitchen specifically, the doors to most of the cupboards have fallen off. The students here are much younger (18-22) and they seem less independent – both financially and emotionally – from their families, which I believe to mean that a lot of them have poor hygiene and do not really care for where they live as they return home every summer – so be warned haha.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember it well. But I think we just had to send a personal statement and give them some official documents such as passport copies and the like. It was easy, just follow their instructions.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not need any help so I do not know.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the ones I wanted. I also took French, which does not count towards my KU courses, I just wanted to learn a new language for free and I would recommend other to do the same. You do not need to pass the course, just have fun with it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Just play around with the schedule builder on Minerva so your classes do not clash. There is also an add and drop period at the start of the semester so your classes are in no way set in stone. Just try different ones. 

I would also recommend to avoid classes on Fridays and or Mondays as this allows you to travel over the weekends. Just be aware that the workload at McGill is very intense. I took five subjects including French so I had 13 lessons (1,5 hours each) a week plus homework - which means that the days that you do have class become very long. In my case, I had about 3 or more lessons a day Monday to Thursday.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic programme was good. Everything is really well planned and thought through. However, I thought that the evaluations were more highschool than university as a lot of assignments and exams or midterms were reflections or multiple choice/short answer questions which did not feel very academic. There are lots of those assignments throughout the semester so you end up spending a lot of time on something that is not very difficult but just needs to be done. That was pretty stressfull at times.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As a master student taking bachelor level courses, I thought that a lot of them were really easy. Also see above^

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: McGill has more of an anglo-saxon teaching tradition, which I really liked. Classes were usually more engaging and less lecture like than at home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ANTH 338 Indigenous Studies of Anthropology

POLI 434 History of Political/Social Theory 

POLI 342 Canadian Foreign Policy

POLI 380 Contemporary Chinese Politics

FRSL 103 Near Beginner's French

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really really enjoyed ANTH 338 Indigenous Studies of Anthropology. The professor shared a lot of wisdom and I learned a lot about an important aspect of Canada. As a poli sci student it was also interesting to know more about the discipline of anthropology.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive. I think Canada has to import a lot of food during winter so the quality was low and the prices high. They also don't show the real price at the super market as they add the taxes (approximately 15 percent) at the end. If you go out to eat you also pay tips (again approximately 15 percent) so everything is 30 percent more expensive than you think. Domestic and regional plane tickets are also really expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only was part of the wine society and ski club but they have lots of clubs. I just prioritised socialising, academics, and exploring Montreal.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So so many. Basically anything you can think of they would have a club for. There's a fair - activity's night - at the beginning of the semester where you can meet all the clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Skiing! 
Mustbus is great for day and weekend trips around Canada and north-eastern USA.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
New York city, Toronto, Chicago, Boston, Ottawa, Quebec City 
Skiing 
Hiking 

I spent a month after the semester travelling around Canada. I went to Banff and Jasper (national parks) and Vancouver with my friends. Then I went east to Quebec City and Tadoussac with my mom. I highly recommend

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: So easy. McGill and Montreal are very international.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just start chatting to the people you sit next to on your first day. Canadian are very friendly and sociable. Just say "hey how are you, is this the right class-room, I'm new... where are you from" etc. and it will be easy

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Quebecois French is very different to French French

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The restaurant and bar culture ! So many great places in Montreal and they're packed every weekend

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Bring warm clothes 
2) Stay on top of deadlines 
3) Plan trips to visit new places while you're here

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't let academics consume you. The semester is very condensed and intense so try to have fun as well !

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Travelling. Canada is STUNNNNING

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The cold weather. I though it could be difficult to go out and socialise in January when it was -15 and dark. But just do it. Put on warm clothes and it will be fun. Also, the winter ends and summer in Montreal is gorgeous. Try to stay past the semester if you can. Today (June 3rd) it is 30 degrees and the city is green and lively, there are lots of festivals and I am starting to love the city more.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
